propose-1.name: KORE: Key-Ordered Robust Execution. Coalition plans are left unchanged under execution noise; anytime ALNS repairs only on structural events; coalition slots are leased; plan-version consensus uses CBBA rules. This is a robustness-first Track D design, reshaped by new pilot evidence (see why_it_should_win).
propose-1.benchmark_spec:
DynHeteroMRTA-X. It extends the HeteroMRTA RA-L 2025 benchmark and anchors every perturbation externally where an anchor exists.

WHAT STAYS IDENTICAL TO HeteroMRTA
- Instance generator and the 8 H1 settings of prereg-phase1: SA-BT(25,5,50), SA-BT(50,5,50), SA-AT(50,5,50), MA-AT(25,5,50), MA-AT(50,5,50), and the large settings (50,5,200), (150,10,500), (150,5,500) for scaling.
- Coalition semantics: additive trait cover and minimal covers. A task starts when the covering members are present, and those members are held for its duration.
- Euclidean travel at speed 0.2. Makespan = all tasks finished and all robots at their depots. Cap of 200 (failure = 200).
- The env event loop (DynTaskEnv subclass, 7 overrides, bit-identical to the static env when every perturbation is off; already checked on 5 instances and 15 RL rollouts).
- The published RL checkpoint, unmodified. Unknown tasks and robots are all-zero rows, which the network treats as padding.
- The same dev/test seed bases as the Phase-1 prereg.

DECLARED CHANGES
- Arrival-order coalitions. Regression test: identical to decision-order under ideal comms.
- Causal observations: nominal ETA plus stall so far. The oracle leak is removed.
- Departure back-dating is capped at the last release.
- Idle robots wait in place and go home at the end.
- A fail_agent override.
- A real-time loop (T below).

PERTURBATION FAMILIES (CRN keyed by instance and seed, so every method sees the same realization)
- N, travel delays: the LoRR 2026 Start-Kit DelayGenerator (MIT; verified in source). Each tick, each available agent starts a stall with probability pDelay (Bernoulli), lasting Uniform{min..max} ticks.
  - N1 = the Start-Kit example {0.01, 1-4}; N3 = {0.05, 1-10}; N4 = {0.05, 10-50}.
  - 1 tick = env dt 0.1 = the LoRR actionMoveTimeLimit default of 100 ms (driver.cpp).
- D, durations: mean-preserving lognormal, sigma 0.3 or 0.6 (convention). Sensitivity: exponential and U(0,2d) (stochastic-RCPSP convention, Ballestin and Leus 2009).
- R, online release:
  - R1 = the HeteroMRTA authors' own reactive-planning demo in plot_animation (ids <= 20 at t=0, +20 every 10 time units). This is the strongest anchor.
  - R2/R3 = DVRP degree of dynamism 0.5/0.8, uniform order statistics on [0, H], H = 0.5 x the paper's RL(g.) makespan. The total task count is known. The station at the map centre is the dispatch source.
- F, fail-stop robot failures:
  - Each robot fails with probability p_f in {0.1, 0.2} at a time drawn from U[0, 0.7 x the instance's nominal ALNS makespan]. The robot halts and its task in progress is aborted (restarted from scratch when re-covered).
  - Detection by heartbeat timeout h = 5 ticks under good comms.
  - Realizations that make any task infeasible are excluded, paired, for all methods.
  - Anchor is weak: event types follow D-ITAGS (RA-L 2023); the rates follow the failure sweeps of Gosrich et al. (T-RO 2025). Declared as a convention.
- C, communication (for C3 only; the robustness-first primary is global instant comms):
  - Unit-disk range R in {inf, 1.3, 1.0, 0.75} x r_c(n).
  - Per-message loss: Bernoulli p in {0.1, 0.3}; Gilbert-Elliott two-state per-link calendar (CV_MRTA / cbja parameters, mean good 12 s / bad 3 s); Rayleigh distance-dependent (CV_MRTA protocol).
  - Latency 1 tick. Per-link calendars in absolute time plus per-(link, send-tick) uniforms give CRN. cbja/network.py is used only as a small-case oracle.
- T, real-time loop: the LoRR 2026 two-rate loop (verified: planCommTimeLimit 1000 ms, initialPlanTimeLimit 1000 ms, actionMoveTimeLimit 100 ms; while the planner is late, robots execute the last staged actions).
  - Every planner or policy call, RL forward passes included, is charged its measured 1-core wall-clock time rounded up to 100 ms ticks, capped at 1000 ms.
  - Robots execute the staged plan meanwhile.
  - Sensitivity: 1 tick = 1 s, where compute is almost free.

SCENARIO FAMILIES FOR ENDPOINTS
- F0 noise only {N1, N2 = D0.3, N3, N4}: a control. Parity is expected (see evidence).
- F1 release {R1, R2, R3}.
- F2 release + noise {R1+N3, R2+N3}.
- F3 failures {Fp.1, Fp.2, Fp.2+N3}.
- C3 grid: F2 and F3 crossed with the C conditions D1 (Bernoulli 0.3, R = 1.3 r_c), D2 (Gilbert-Elliott, R = r_c; the primary degraded condition) and D3 (R = 0.75 r_c).

METRICS
- Makespan (primary); success and completion; P90 makespan.
- CPU per event and per episode; re-plans or decisions per episode.
- Mean wait at coalition tasks; abandonments and wasted trips; plan churn.
- Messages and bytes (C3).
- Gap to a clairvoyant reference: release-aware hindsight ALNS on realized durations, start >= release; not defined for failures.

SEEDS
- Dev: 20 instances per setting (pilots and tuning only).
- Test: 50 instances x 3 CRN seeds. The noise, release, failure and channel seeds all equal the CRN seed.
- ALNS seed per call = 1000 x seed + call index.

Pilot tools already built:
- pilots/trackD/dyn_env.py (env)
- pilots/trackD_robust/rh_pilot.py and rel_pilot.py (fast plan executor with delays, release and state-start ALNS). These must be regression-tested against DynTaskEnv before any claim.
propose-1.algorithm_spec:
KORE runs per robot on 1 CPU core and needs no GPU.

1. INITIAL PLAN
- Phase-1 anytime coalition ALNS on the tasks released at t=0.
- Budget = the LoRR initialPlanTimeLimit, 1000 ms on 1 core.
- Output: minimal-cover coalitions plus a global key order. The plan is broadcast and each robot holds a replica.

2. EXECUTION RULE (local, no planner in the loop)
- Each robot follows its route in key order, departs when free, waits at a coalition task, and the task starts when the present robots cover the requirement.
- Noise events (finishes, stalls, early or late arrivals) never trigger re-planning: they shift times but leave the plan's precedence DAG unchanged.
- A task is COMMITTED once any member has departed to it. Its coalition is then frozen.

3. LEASED COALITION SLOTS
- On departing to coalition task j, robot i holds a lease e_ij = t + max(0, Q0.9[ETA of its slowest believed partner] - t) + delta, with delta = 5 ticks.
  - ETAs come from the calibrated renewal model of the LoRR stalls (travel x kappa, kappa = 1/(1 - stall fraction)) and the conditional residual-life mean for tasks that are still running.
- Partner heartbeats carrying a new ETA renew the lease, capped at tau_max = 3 x the nominal lead time.
- If the lease expires, or a partner's heartbeat times out, without the coalition forming: i abandons j, broadcasts abandon(i, j), continues with its own next task, and j becomes an ORPHAN.

4. STRUCTURAL-EVENT REPAIR (the only place the planner runs)
- Triggers: task release, orphan (failure or abandon), a robot rejoining after a partition.
- Repair region: all released, uncommitted tasks, plus new and orphaned tasks.
- State: a state-start forward pass. ready_i and pos_i are predicted with the calibrated predictors; committed chains are fixed anchors.
- Search:
  - Regret insertion of the new or orphaned tasks.
  - Then warm-started ALNS (the state-start kernel: first leg dout[i,t] = ready_i + travel(pos_i, t)) with a deadline-based budget b = 25 ms per event on 1 core (about 300 iterations at 50 tasks). The anytime result is returned at the deadline.
- New and repaired tasks get keys greater than every committed key, so the union of the old and new orders stays acyclic.

5. REPLICATION AND CONSENSUS (CBBA lineage: this is the consensus layer, not the optimizer)
- The robot or station that detects an event computes the repair and broadcasts a plan delta {j: (members_j, key_j)}.
- Each delta carries a version (t_event, proposer_id), a Lamport-style stamp.
- Receivers merge per task by maximum version. This is CBBA's timestamp rule, i.e. an LWW-register CRDT, so merging is a join.
- A robot that loses a task it holds to a higher version releases every later task in its route (CBBA's bundle-release rule) and triggers a local repair.
- A robot departs to a coalition task only when it has heard each partner acknowledge a version >= its own for that task. Otherwise it waits under its lease.
- Under good comms, all of this equals a central re-solve with structural triggers.

6. CLOSURE-LOCAL REPAIR (degraded comms only)
- When the proposer or station is unreachable, a connected component repairs only tasks whose current and candidate members all lie inside the component. Everything else stays frozen on the last plan, which remains valid under noise because of rule 2.

7. OPTIONAL MODULES (ablations only, not claimed)
- SAA acceptance over S=8 CRN scenarios.
- q80 buffered durations.
- Stability gate (adopt a repair only if its predicted gain exceeds eps).
- Redundant spare members for tail tasks (k-of-n cover).
- Multiple-scenario phantom-task anticipation for releases (Bent and Van Hentenryck).
- A deviation trigger for severe noise (N4).

Pilot code: pilots/trackD_robust/rel_pilot.py (ES methods = rule 2 + rule 4 under good comms).
propose-1.baselines:
Equal infrastructure for every baseline:
- The same env, CRN, event notifications (release, failure detection at heartbeat timeout), causal information and calibrated predictors.
- The same LoRR real-time charge and the same 1-core per-call budget.
- The same gossip layer under C3.

B1. Published RL policy online
- RL(g.) and RL(s.1), checkpoint unmodified. Unknown tasks and failed robots are zero rows. It receives failure notifications.
- Under C3 its observation is built from a belief CRDT fed by the same gossip.
- RL(s.N) best-of-N is not an online policy under noise, so it is excluded, as the scouts noted.

B2. Paper greedy, with the HeteroMRTA dist bug fixed, online.

B3. Central rolling-horizon ALNS (the same engine as KORE)
- (a) Idealized: re-plan at every finish and structural event, 3000 iterations, zero latency.
- (b) Best trigger policy chosen on dev, which will be structural-only, making it identical to KORE under good comms.
- (c) Under C3: CEN-F = the station re-plans the robots in its component; everyone else follows the last plan with leases (local fallback).

B4. Replicated solver + event gossip (REP): every robot runs the same seeded ALNS on its belief after each event it hears; the newest version wins.

B5. RH-CP-SAT-LNS (our Phase-1 CP-SAT-LNS with constructor hints), at the same per-event budget and at 1000 ms.

B6. RH-constructor: regret insertion with restarts filling the per-event budget. This is the "simple rule" re-planner.

B7. CBBA-family coalition auctions, re-run to consensus on each structural event
- CBTA-style timetable consensus (Wang et al., RA-L 2022), CBGA-style grouping (Hunt et al., 2014), coupled-constraint CBBA with optimistic and pessimistic bidding (Whitten et al., ACC 2011). All reimplemented and disclosed as such.
- Bids use OUR insertion kernel, the strongest bid function available, so they are not strawmen.

B8. Proactive robust baselines, each run open-loop and with KORE's repair:
- Messing et al. RSS 2023-style sampled-scenario robust coalition schedule (ALNS whose plan must satisfy K sampled scenarios).
- q80 buffered durations.

B9. D-ITAGS-style targeted repair (RA-L 2023): insertion plus local LNS restricted to the coalitions directly touched by the event.

B10. References, not competitors:
- Clairvoyant hindsight ALNS.
- RH-orc (perfect duration foresight).
- Open loop (with release this equals insertion-only repair).

CTAS-D has no dynamic rows and is cited only for the static part.
propose-1.why_it_should_win:
Honest answer: KORE should clearly beat RL, the auctions, the insertion rule and CP-SAT-LNS. It will NOT beat a central re-planner that uses our own engine with good triggers under good comms; that comparison is parity by construction. Execution noise cannot supply a margin: open loop is within about 2% of re-planning, anticipation is worth about 1-2%, and the 2-10% gap to clairvoyance is out of reach for any causal policy. The only open door to a win over the strongest baseline is C3, and it is unproven.

The pilots were run during this session on dev instances: 4 settings x 10 instances x 2 CRN seeds = 80 paired episodes per cell. They use the plan executor (not yet the env), snapshot ALNS v1, and a loaded shared host. Outputs are in pilots/trackD_robust/out/c2 and out/rel; summarizers are summarize_c2.py and summarize_rel.py.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS
(1) Against the published RL online, a clear margin.
- Under noise: RL(g.) / RH-ALNS = 1.205, 1.230, 1.221 (N2, N3, N4; RL wins 0-2 of 80).
- Under release: RL(g.) / KORE at 3 ms per event = 1.151-1.167 (R1, R2, R3, R2+N3; RL wins 0-7 of 80, the 7 all in the release-bound SA-BT R1 cell).
- So KORE is about 14-19% better. RL degrades little under noise, but it starts roughly 20% behind. This margin is mostly the known static quality gap, and must be reported that way.
(2) Against insertion-based repair, a clear margin, and this is the part that is not a simple rule.
- Insertion-only repair / ALNS repair = 1.070, 1.122, 1.113, 1.132 in R1, R2, R3, R2+N3.
- This is the ceiling of a CBBA-family insertion auction started from our own strong t=0 plan. A CBTA or CBGA auction planning from scratch should lose at least this much.
(3) Against RH-CP-SAT-LNS at 10-1000 ms per event: expected 2-11%, from the static matched-compute results. CP-SAT cannot build and solve its model in 25 ms.
(4) Compute (C2): a strong result.
- Per re-plan: ALNS 300 iterations = 13 ms, within 0.998-1.018 of 3000 iterations (122 ms). 30 iterations = 3 ms, within 1.019-1.034.
- Repairing only on structural events beats re-planning at every event by 1.1-1.9% (R1-R3; tie under R2+N3) with 2.5x fewer re-plans (23 vs 57 per episode).
(5) Paired with the rows above: the paper greedy is 33-37% worse.

WHERE IT WILL NOT WIN (the robustness-first premise is refuted under good comms)
- Re-planning does not help under noise. Open loop / RH-ALNS at 3000 iterations = 0.993 [0.977, 1.009], 0.999 [0.981, 1.015], 1.022 [1.002, 1.043] (N2, N3, N4).
- Cheap re-planning is harmful (nervousness). RH at 30 iterations / open loop = 1.042 and 1.051 (N2, N3).
- A stability gate does not fix it. Gated re-planning at 300 iterations, eps 0.5% / open loop = 1.026, 1.024, 1.000. Adopted re-plans predicted to be better are worse in reality; the likely cause is residual-duration bias in the predictor.
- The value of information is large but out of reach. RH / RH with perfect duration foresight = 1.101, 1.023, 1.016. No causal policy can capture this.
- Anticipation is small. The earlier lever pilot measured nominal plan / SAA-selected plan = 0.999-1.022, and q80 buffers were worse (0.95-0.99).
- So proactive or robust plans can add at most about 1-2%, and a central RH that uses our engine and structural triggers IS KORE under good comms.

WHERE A WIN IS STILL POSSIBLE BUT UNPROVEN (C3)
- Rule 2 makes stale replicas valid under noise. Only about 23 structural events per episode need dissemination. Leases bound the damage from inconsistent coalitions, and closure-local repair acts on failures detected inside a partition.
- The prior integrated pilot (heuristic planner, aggressive local re-planning) found local repair worse than central-with-fallback and than keeping the plan at low range. Whether KORE's keep-the-plan design reverses that is the main open risk.
propose-1.collapse_check:
Analytical view
- For a key-ordered plan, the realized makespan is the longest path in a fixed DAG with random weights (a max-plus linear system).
- Noise events reveal independent, memoryless information: LoRR stalls are Bernoulli per tick, and durations are independent across tasks. Re-planning can therefore only exploit second-order state shifts, which is why re-planning ties or loses under noise.
- Structural events (release, failure) change the problem by a first-order amount, so a greedy local rule (insertion) repairs them badly. That is where search pays. This matches the pilots (items 1 and 2 below).
- The parts of KORE that ARE simple rules are declared as design rules, not claimed as mechanisms:
  - no re-planning on noise;
  - commit at departure;
  - calibrated lease margin;
  - under good comms, lease expiry collapses to heartbeat timeout.

Prespecified collapse tests (all reported whatever the outcome)
- T1, repair versus rule: KORE vs KORE-insertion-only on F1, F2 and F3.
  - Pass if KORE is better by >= 3% with the CI excluding 0 on >= 3 of 4 settings.
  - Pilot so far: 7-13%.
  - If < 1%, the method is "static ALNS plus insertion" and no dynamic-method claim is made.
- T2, trigger rule: KORE vs RH at every event, same engine and budget. Expected: KORE <= RH by 1-2%. This is reported as a design rule, not a mechanism.
- T3, noise-only control: KORE's decisions equal open loop in 100% of noise events by construction. Its makespan vs RH-ALNS is tested by TOST +/-2%. Parity is the honest outcome.
- T4: stability gate and T5: proactive SAA, buffers, spares and phantom tasks. Each is an ablation that must give >= 2% with the CI excluding 0 to enter the method. The prior is negative: the gate gave +2.4-2.6% worse, and anticipation is <= 2%.
- T6, decision-difference log vs a central re-solve with structural triggers:
  - Good comms: expected 0%, i.e. identical.
  - Degraded comms: if KORE's adopted repairs differ from the central planner's in < 5% of structural events, any C3 gain cannot come from the mechanism and is not claimed.
- T7, leases: tau = infinity vs fixed tau vs calibrated tau, under F3 and C3. Under good comms, expect >= 95% agreement with heartbeat detection (declared collapse). Leases must earn their place in F3 x D2 through success rate or P90 makespan.
- T8, CBBA consensus layer vs "newest version wins without bundle release":
  - Under good comms, identical.
  - Under D2/D3, the number of inconsistent coalitions and wasted trips must drop with the CI excluding 0. Otherwise the CBBA lineage is only nominal and is described that way.
propose-1.pilot_plan:
ALREADY DONE (this session, dev, not committed)
- P1 noise re-planning, out/c2: open loop ties RH; cheap RH loses 3-5%.
- P2 release, out/rel: structural-only ALNS repair beats every-event RH by 1-2%, beats insertion by 7-13%, 13 ms per event suffices, and RL is 14-19% worse.
- P3 stability gate, out/c2/gate.jsonl: no help.
- Scripts: pilots/trackD_robust/{rel_pilot.py, gate_pilot.py, summarize_c2.py, summarize_rel.py}.
- Earlier lever pilot: anticipation <= 2%.

1-WEEK PLAN
Days 1-2, environment fidelity
- Port the KORE executor onto DynTaskEnv, or show equivalence: executor makespan == env replay on 20 episodes per family, to 1e-6 for plans with minimal covers.
- Add fail_agent, arrival-order coalitions (regression: equal to decision-order under ideal comms), the LoRR real-time charge, and the release-aware hindsight bound.
- Kill K0: equivalence fails and cannot be fixed within 2 days -> all pilot numbers are provisional; stop and fix before anything else.

Days 2-3, failures pilot (F3; 4 settings x 10 dev instances x 2 seeds)
- Methods: KORE at 25 ms, insertion-only, RH at 3000, RL(g.) with failure notification, greedy; lease variants.
- K1: KORE / RL(g.) > 0.90 pooled over F1-F3, or KORE / insertion-only > 0.98 on F3 -> dynamics do not separate methods beyond the static gap. Drop the dynamic-method claim; Track D becomes an analysis section.

Days 3-4, baselines
- Build B5 (RH-CP-SAT-LNS), B6, B7 (CBTA, CBGA, coupled-constraint CBBA with our insertion bids), B8 (Messing-style robust schedule) and B9 (D-ITAGS-style repair).
- K2: any non-ALNS baseline within 2% of KORE on F1 (the CI includes 0.98) -> it is a simple-rule equivalent, and the KORE claim reduces to "the Phase-1 ALNS in the loop".

Days 4-5, C3 pilot on MA-AT-25 and SA-BT-50 (the two extremes)
- Conditions D1-D3 x {F2, F3}.
- Methods: KORE, CEN-F, REP, open loop + leases + station insertion, RL on beliefs.
- Log messages, inconsistencies and the T6 decision differences.
- K3: at D2, KORE / min(CEN-F, REP) is not < 0.98 with the CI excluding 1 in both settings -> no C3 superiority. Report TOST parity and messages only. The RA-L Track D claim then shrinks to C2 plus robustness guarantees.

Day 5, real-time loop
- KORE at {0, 3, 25, 100, 1000} ms per event under the 100 ms-tick latency charge, with RL latency charged too.
- K4: 25 ms is more than 2% worse than the best budget -> the "light" claim is weakened; re-tune the budget on dev.

Day 6, scale
- MA-AT-50-5-200, and 150x500 with compact observations and RL on GPU. KORE must keep per-event time under 100 ms on 1 core.
- K5: if not, restrict the claims to <= 200 tasks.

Day 7
- Write docs/trackD-spec.md (endpoints, margins, families, seeds).
- Freeze the solver commit and run the test split once on a quiet, pinned host.

Engineering note
- All pilot timings came from a shared host at load 40-100. My pilots ran 32 processes from 00:35 to 00:55 UTC, alongside ALNS v1/v2 timing task #2, whose timings from that window may be perturbed.
propose-1.prereg_endpoints:
Unit of analysis: paired per (setting, test instance, CRN seed). Statistic: r = makespan(KORE) / makespan(competitor), with failure counted as 200. Report the mean of log r, the bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 0), win counts and the success rate.

E1 (C1-dyn, primary superiority)
- Families F1, F2, F3 under good comms with the real-time charge.
- KORE at 25 ms per event on 1 core vs each of: RL(g.) online, paper greedy, CBTA-style, CBGA-style, coupled-constraint CBBA, RH-CP-SAT-LNS (same budget, and at 1000 ms), RH-constructor, D-ITAGS-style repair, and the Messing-style robust schedule with repair.
- One-sided paired t-test of mean log r < 0, Holm-corrected over settings x families x competitors.
- Expected: RL about 0.84-0.87; auctions and D-ITAGS-style repair <= 0.95.

E2 (C1-dyn, parity by design)
- KORE vs central RH-ALNS (same engine, 3000 iterations, zero latency, best trigger chosen on dev) on F1-F3.
- TOST with margin +/-2% (|mean log r| < 0.0198), alpha 0.05 per family.
- Also reported: vs every-event RH (expected 0.98-0.99).

E3 (C2)
- Anytime curve of KORE's per-event budget {0, 3, 25, 100, 1000 ms}.
- Primary: KORE at 25 ms vs KORE at 1000 ms, TOST +/-2%, on F1-F3.
- Secondary: time for KORE to reach RH-CP-SAT-LNS-at-1000-ms quality; CPU seconds per episode.
- Under the latency charge: KORE at 25 ms is not worse than any budget >= 100 ms (one-sided, margin 1%).

E4 (C3, primary degraded condition D2; D1 and D3 secondary)
- KORE vs CEN-F and vs REP (same engine and triggers) on F2 and F3.
- Superiority: one-sided, Holm-corrected, mean log r < 0.
- Co-primary: degradation ratio makespan(D2) / makespan(good comms) for KORE is lower than for both.
- Secondary: messages and bytes per episode, success rate and P90 makespan.
- If superiority fails: TOST +/-3% reported as parity.

E5 (robustness under failures, F3)
- Success rate of KORE non-inferior to the best competitor (margin 1 pp).
- P90 makespan ratio.
- Lease ablation (tau = infinity, fixed, calibrated) on success rate and wasted wait.

E6 (collapse and control, reported descriptively)
- T1-T8 as in collapse_check.
- F0 noise-only parity vs RH (TOST +/-2%).
- Clairvoyant gap per family.

Decision rule
- Track D enters the RA-L paper as a method contribution only if E1 holds on >= 80% of setting x family cells against every competitor, E3 holds, and T1 passes.
- C3 is claimed only if E4 superiority holds at D2. Otherwise Track D is reported as real-time robust execution with parity against central re-solve.
propose-1.guarantees:
Stated with their assumptions. There is no optimality guarantee; the gap to the clairvoyant reference is reported instead.

(G1) Deadlock freedom
- Assumptions: arbitrary finite travel delays and durations, and consistent replicas.
- Claim: every coalition task eventually starts.
- Reason: execution follows a global key order, and every repair assigns keys greater than all committed keys, so the precedence graph stays acyclic. This is the same argument as ADG for MAPF (Hoenig et al., RA-L 2019) and the serial schedule-generation scheme in RCPSP. It is not novel.

(G2) Bounded waiting
- No robot waits longer than tau_max plus one heartbeat period at any coalition task, under fail-stop failures and message loss, because leases have a hard cap.

(G3) Liveness under fail-stop failures with eventually-delivered messages
- Claim: every released task whose requirement is coverable by live robots is eventually completed.
- Reason: each abandonment or failure creates an orphan; orphans trigger repair; repair returns a feasible plan at any budget (insertion first, measured at about 2 ms); the number of failures is finite.

(G4) Replica convergence
- The per-task maximum-version merge is a join-semilattice (an LWW-register CRDT), so replicas that receive the same set of deltas converge regardless of order.
- Under partitions, inconsistent coalitions are possible (Two Generals), but by G2 their cost is bounded by the lease.

(G5) Anytime
- The repair returns a feasible, key-ordered plan at any deadline no shorter than the insertion time.
propose-1.risks:
1. MAIN RISK, the premise fails: under good comms the robustness-first angle has no headroom (evidence above).
- KORE ties a central re-planner that uses our engine. Its RL margin is mostly the static solver gap.
- Reviewers can say "this is RH with your Phase-1 ALNS". The only defensible novelties are the empirical findings (noise does not justify re-planning; structural repair needs search) plus C3.

2. C3 is unproven and has a negative prior.
- The integrated pilot found local re-planning worse than central-with-fallback and than keeping the plan at R <= 0.15.
- If K3 fires, Track D has no superiority claim over central re-solve.

3. Fidelity: all new numbers come from a hand-written plan executor, not DynTaskEnv.
- Known differences: idle robots go home vs wait in place; back-dating; decision-order vs arrival-order.
- The RL rows came from DynTaskEnv under the same CRN keys. The executor-vs-env equivalence (K0) must pass before any claim.

4. Weak anchors.
- R2/R3 Poisson release, lognormal durations and the failure model are conventions. Only LoRR delays, the LoRR real-time loop, R1 (the authors' demo) and the CV_MRTA channel protocol are external.
- There are no published dynamic HeteroMRTA numbers to compare with.
- DODRL-HMRTA (Neurocomputing 2026) and the CSCWD 2026 fault-recovery paper still could not be read; web searches found neither. Both must be checked before claiming the dynamic-HeteroMRTA gap.

5. Prior art covers every component: ADG/SADG (key order), D-ITAGS (targeted repair), Messing et al. RSS 2023 (sampled-scenario robust coalition scheduling), Policella et al. (partial-order schedules), Prorok et al. (redundant assignment, T-ASE 2020), Bent and Van Hentenryck (multiple-scenario approach), CC-OPI (versioned sets and locks), CBTA/CBGA (coalition auctions). Novelty is empirical and comes from the combination.

6. Predictor bias. The re-plan harm under noise may come from the residual-life bias of nominal predictions. If a better predictor makes RH win under noise, the baselines get it too (equal infrastructure) and parity remains. Rule 2 might then need a deviation trigger.

7. CBBA lineage is thin. The auction component loses 7-13% as an optimizer, so the CBBA contribution is only the consensus layer, which matters only under C3.

8. Baselines B7-B9 are reimplementations: there is no official code for CBTA, CBGA, D-ITAGS or Messing. Use the strongest bid and insertion functions available and disclose this.

9. Compute evidence comes from a heavily loaded host and snapshot ALNS v1. Per-event times must be re-measured on a quiet, pinned core with v2. My runs may have perturbed concurrent timing task #2 between 00:35 and 00:55 UTC.

10. At large scale (150x500), RL needs GPU batching and KORE's per-event time is unmeasured (K5).

propose-2.name: SCOPE-RALNS: partition-scoped rolling coalition ALNS with CRDT event gossip. This is the comm-first Track D design, with the communication layer reduced by pilot evidence to a deliberately simple rule.
propose-2.benchmark_spec:
HeteroMRTA-DC (dynamic, communication-limited). It is one extension of the published benchmark, not a new world.

WHAT STAYS IDENTICAL TO HeteroMRTA (marmotlab @db51e29, Apache-2.0)
- Instance generator, traits, requirements, durations, speed 0.2, dt 0.1.
- Makespan definition: all tasks finished and every robot back at its depot; the 200 cap counts as failure.
- Coalition semantics, and the released RL checkpoint, unmodified.
- Ground truth is DynTaskEnv, the subclass of TaskEnv already built by the env scout (bit-identical to the static env when every release is at 0 and there is no noise). A CommLayer is added to it.
- Regression tests: with ideal comm, the arrival-order coalitions of the comm layer must equal the env's decision-order coalitions (plan replay and RL rollouts bit-identical). The surrogate world used in today's pilots (pilots/trackD/integ_headroom.py) is not a results world.

SETTINGS AND SEEDS
- Primary: MA-AT-25-5-50, MA-AT-50-5-50, SA-AT-50-5-50, SA-BT-50-5-50 (the 50-task H1 settings). Secondary: MA-AT-50-5-200.
- Test split per prereg: seed 100000+1000·idx+i, i<50. Dev split for all tuning.
- 3 common-random-number (CRN) seeds per instance, keyed by (seed, instance, entity), identical for every method: release times, duration noise, per-agent delay calendars in absolute time, and per-link per-tick loss uniforms.

PERTURBATIONS (external anchors)
- Release:
  - R2: Poisson, degree of dynamism 0.5 on H = 0.5 × paper RL(g.) makespan (the DVRP convention).
  - R1: the authors' own batch-release demo in the released code (ids ≤20 at t=0, +20 every 10 time units).
  - R3: degree of dynamism 0.8.
  - New tasks become known at a dispatch station at (0.5, 0.5), as in D-CTS/LFB-style dispatch, and spread by gossip.
- Execution noise:
  - LoRR 2026 Start-Kit DelayGenerator (verified in source): Bernoulli pDelay 0.01, 1–4 ticks (the example config); moderate 0.05, 1–10.
  - Mean-preserving lognormal durations, σ = 0.3.
- Communication:
  - Unit-disk range R set as a multiple of the random-geometric-graph connectivity radius r_c(n) = sqrt(ln n / (π n)) (Penrose 2003; Gupta & Kumar 1998), not in arbitrary absolute units: R/r_c ∈ {∞, 2.0, 1.25, 1.0, 0.75, 0.6}. For n=25, r_c = 0.202; for n=50, r_c = 0.158.
  - Link loss from the CV_MRTA benchmark (arXiv 2609.13711; the protocol is reimplemented because the code has no license):
    - Bernoulli p = 0.25 (the Lott & Honary 25% condition);
    - Gilbert–Elliott;
    - Rayleigh distance-dependent success.
  - Multi-hop flooding inside a connected component within one tick.
  - Robots observe task start and finish on site.
  - t=0 briefing with full comm (tasks released at 0 and the initial plan).
- Agent failures (secondary): fail-stop of 10% of robots at uniform times in [0, H/2], detected by heartbeat lease.
- Declared unit mapping (a convention, not an anchor): unit square side = 1 km, 1 time unit = 100 s, so speed is 2 m/s, a LoRR tick is 10 s, and R = r_c(50) is 158 m.

CONDITIONS
- Primary condition P: RN12, i.e. R2 release + σ = 0.3 + LoRR example delays, at R = 1.0 r_c with Bernoulli 0.25 loss. Fixed a priori at the canonical connectivity threshold, not tuned.
- Secondary conditions: the R sweep, RN3, R1, GE, Rayleigh, failures, and the 200-task setting.
- The CC-OPI warning is confirmed by pilot: with R ≥ 1.5 r_c, 20% loss leaves every re-planner within 2–4% of full information. Range and partitions are the stressor, not loss.

METRICS
- Makespan; success; degradation D(m) = makespan(m, P) / makespan(m, ideal comm, same noise and release).
- Gap to FULL (same method with ideal comm) and to a clairvoyant offline ALNS (releases and realized durations known).
- Redundant trips, abandons.
- Route-version messages and bytes per robot per time unit.
- Per-event CPU time on 1 pinned core (median, p95).
propose-2.algorithm_spec:
SCOPE-RALNS. Each robot (and the station) runs the same code. CBBA lineage: a consensus layer with CBBA-style timestamp conflict resolution, and a bundle builder that is replaced by coalition LNS with partial (tail) replanning, as in CBBA-PR (Buckman, How, Choi 2019).

1. Replicated state as a delta-state CRDT, merged on contact by anti-entropy over version vectors
   - Task released: a grow-only set carrying the task data.
   - Task start and finish times: min-registers.
   - Per-(robot, task) abandon records: grow-only.
   - Per-robot physical record (mode, target, ETA or finish time, position): last-writer-wins on that robot's own Lamport counter.
   - Per-robot route version: last-writer-wins on (Lamport epoch, author id). This is the CBBA max-consensus rule on timestamps.
   - Merge is commutative, associative and idempotent. Messages carry events and route deltas only, O(decisions), never full tables.

2. Planning scope (the communication rule; selected by pilot, not by design preference)
   - A component leader plans. The leader is the station if it is in the component, otherwise the lowest robot id among the heartbeat-live members.
   - It plans only for robots in its own component.
   - A robot outside the component contributes only its physically committed head task: the task it is travelling to or waiting at. Its traits are subtracted from that task's requirement.
   - It is never given new work, and its believed future route is ignored, not frozen.
   - Redundant service across partitions is tolerated: a task starts when the robots present cover it, in arrival order, and late arrivals leave (a wasted trip).
   - Optional ablation, hyperparameter θ ≥ 0 (DTHθ): a robot outside the component is also planned for, with ready time τ_i, if its predicted information-arrival delay τ_i − now ≤ θ. τ_i is computed by epidemic temporal-BFS flooding over the robots' believed trajectories: 0.5 time-unit grid, horizon 40, idle robots predicted to rally to the station. θ = 0 is pure component scope (INF-r); θ = ∞ is the replicated solver REP+. θ ∈ {0, 1, 3} is tuned on dev; the default is θ = 0 unless another θ wins by ≥ 2% with p < 0.05 on dev.

3. Planner: warm-started rolling coalition ALNS
   - Phase-1 kernels, state-start copy: agent i is free at ready[i] at pos[i], first leg dout, key-ordered minimal covers.
   - Triggers: a new task known, a task start, finish or abandon, a change of component membership, and a period of 1.0 time unit.
   - Coalition commitment: a task's coalition is frozen once its first member departs, if all its members are in the leader's component. A coalition that spans a partition boundary is not frozen: its reachable members stay re-plannable, its unreachable members keep their heads.
   - A committed head still missing traits is re-planned with its residual requirement.
   - Agents become ready at the predicted (nominal) finish of their committed chain.
   - Warm start: the component's merged incumbent restricted to uncommitted tasks, with invalid members dropped.
   - Budget: 300 iterations (about 20 ms at 50 tasks; C2); anytime sweep 30 to 1000.
   - New route versions are authored only for robots whose route changed. Hysteresis is implicit because the search is warm-started.
   - Objective: lexicographic (tasks placed, makespan + λ·mean finish).

4. Execution
   - A robot departs to its next route task when its head finishes.
   - Arrival-order start.
   - ETA-based lease: a waiting robot abandons when no robot it believes is coming arrives within grace g = 1.0, or when its wait exceeds (latest believed partner ETA − now) + margin m. There is no fixed cap: in the pilot, a fixed 10-unit cap turned a 49.6 open-loop plan into 69.0 through 26 cascading abandons. An abandon authors a self-version and broadcasts an abandon event.
   - Rally rule (shared by all methods): an idle robot with an empty route that is disconnected from the station moves toward the station until connected.

5. Compute: CPU only, numba kernels, one core per robot; no GPU anywhere in the method.
propose-2.baselines:
All baselines run in the same DynTaskEnv+CommLayer, with the same CRDT gossip, ETA leases and rally rule, and the same per-event CPU budget. Every planning baseline uses the same rolling ALNS where applicable, so the arms differ only in the stated factor.

1. References (not competitors)
   - FULL-RALNS: ideal communication.
   - Clairvoyant offline ALNS: releases and realized durations known in advance.

2. Central rolling re-solve with local fallback (CEN-F)
   - The station re-plans the robots it can reach. Unreachable robots keep their last route, then rally.
   - Two planners: CEN-F-RALNS on 1 core, and CEN-F with our CP-SAT-LNS on 8 cores at 1 s per event (the "heavy central" C2 contrast).

3. Replicated solver with event gossip (REP+)
   - Every component leader plans for ALL robots on its belief; the newest version wins.
   - Stale robots' free times are clamped to now. Without this fix the naive REP lets the planner believe stale robots can arrive in the past, which cost 2–9% in the pilot.
   - This is the strongest "plan for everyone" baseline.

4. Published RL, run online and decentralized (RL-dec)
   - The released checkpoint runs on each robot's own CRDT belief. Unknown tasks and agents are zero rows, which the network treats exactly as padding (checked: max |Δp| 7.8e-7).
   - Same leases and rally rule. RL(s.N) best-of-N is not legal online.

5. CBBA family (disclosed reimplementations; no code exists)
   - CBTA (Wang et al., RA-L 2022): timetable consensus for simultaneous multi-agent tasks, asynchronous within components (ACBBA-style), with CBBA-PR partial reset of the last k bundle items on events. Run with its native objective (average start time) and with a makespan variant.
   - Coupled-constraint CBBA (Whitten et al. 2011), with its partner-wait iteration limits converted to leases.

6. Simple-rule planners (planner collapse)
   - Our regret-insertion constructor, re-run cold at every event (RH-constructor).
   - The integ world's earliest-start list-scheduling dispatcher (8 noisy restarts, hysteresis).
   - The paper greedy, bug-fixed (the dist update).

7. Communication-collapse arms (ablations; all use the same planner)
   - LOC-F: component planning with the outsiders' believed routes frozen. This is the original "frozen prefix" proposal.
   - FRZk: bundle length k ∈ {2, 3}, after Lott & Honary 2026.
   - DAR: delivery-aware frozen prefix up to τ_i.
   - DAR-r: τ_i ready time only.
   - CSRc: τ_i = now + c.
   - DTHθ.
   - INF-r (θ = 0) is the method's default and is reported as the simple rule it is.
   - REP (naive).

8. OPEN: the static plan with insertion of new tasks only.
propose-2.why_it_should_win:
The communication mechanism itself will NOT beat the strongest communication baseline by a clear margin. The method is INF-r (or ties it), and it beats REP+ only when partitions are severe. The clear margins it should show are planner margins and replicate-per-component margins.

Pilot numbers (dev split, surrogate world, same list-scheduling planner for every arm, 160 pairs per range unless noted). Ratios are method/FULL, so lower is better.
- Well connected, R ≈ 1.5–1.9 r_c: every re-planner is at 1.02–1.04 of FULL. There is no headroom for any decentralized mechanism there.
- Partitioned, R = 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.1 absolute (about 1.0–1.27, 0.74–0.95 and 0.5–0.63 r_c):

| Arm | R = 0.2 | R = 0.15 | R = 0.1 | Success |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| REP+ | 1.072 | 1.205 | 1.391 | 0.96–0.99 |
| INF-r | 1.089 | 1.119 | 1.185 | 1.00 |
| DTH1 | 1.071 | 1.100 | 1.237 | 1.00 |

Expected effect sizes on the primary condition P, per competitor:
- Central re-solve + local fallback (CEN-F), 60 pairs, R = 0.3 / 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.1:
  - INF-r/CEN-F: 0.988 / 0.948 [0.902, 0.992] / 0.921 [0.869, 0.969] / 0.772 [0.728, 0.818].
  - DTH1/CEN-F: 0.988 / 0.924 / 0.907 / 0.792.
  - Expect 5–9% at P and about 20% at 0.6 r_c. Mechanism: every component keeps re-planning, instead of robots out of the station's reach idling or following stale routes.
- Published RL, decentralized: expect ≥ 20%. Most of this is the solver-quality gap: the constructor already beats RL(s.10) by 14–22% statically, ALNS beats it by 21–27%, and open-loop ALNS still beats RL by 18–30% under noise. Reviewers will discount this part.
- CBBA-family coalition auctions: expect about 10%, from planner quality. These auctions are greedy constructors, and in the loop warm rolling ALNS beats the cold constructor by 9.4–9.6%: 0.906 [0.890, 0.923] and 0.904 [0.888, 0.919], 69–73/80 wins, at about 20 ms per re-plan. This is unverified until CBTA is reimplemented.
- Our constructor in the loop: about 9.5% (measured).
- REP+ with the same planner:
  - Parity at R ≥ 1.25 r_c (TOST ±3% plausible).
  - 9–15% better at R ≤ 0.95 r_c: DTH1/REP+ is 0.913 [0.876, 0.947] and 0.889 [0.847, 0.931]. That gain comes from REP+'s failure tails (phantom assignments to unreachable robots) and belongs to the simple scope rule.
- INF-r: no win. DTH1/INF-r is 0.991, 0.983, 0.982 and 1.044 (the last significantly worse).

Bottom line: a paper claiming a new decentralized coordination mechanism is not supported. Track D should be the C3 robustness evidence for the ALNS paper: "anytime coalition LNS stays SOTA when executed online over partitioned networks with a simple scoped CRDT protocol."
propose-2.collapse_check:
Analytic
- DTHθ contains REP+ (θ = ∞) and INF-r (θ = 0) as special cases. DAR contains REP (τ ≡ now) and LOC-F (τ ≡ ∞).
- A predicted delivery time can only help where τ_i is heterogeneous across robots and comparable to task lead times: departure-to-start median 1.7–2.3 time units, flooding delay to all robots 2.5–10 at R ≈ 0.6–1.3 r_c.
- If the network is connected, everything is REP+. If partitions are long, everything is INF-r.
- If τ_i is predictable by a constant, CSRc suffices.

Pilot (done today, dev split). Code: /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD_comm2/dar_pilot.py, planner_collapse.py, summarize3.py. Outputs: /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD_comm2/out/*_summary.txt.

(a) The angle's core, local repair inside frozen prefixes, is refuted. This is the third independent pilot to show it, after the P1 comm_sim and integ_headroom.
- Freezing more is monotonically worse. At R = 0.1, /FULL: FRZ1 1.213, FRZ2 1.435, FRZ3 1.570; CST8 1.865.
- DAR/REP: 1.035 [1.006, 1.065] at R = 0.3 and 1.224 [1.096, 1.388] at R = 0.1.

(b) The delivery-aware ready time collapses.
- DAR-r/REP+: 1.008, 1.023, 0.960 [0.918, 1.003], 0.971.
- CSRc ties DAR-r.
- DAR-r/INF-r: 1.033 and 1.140 at R = 0.15 and 0.1.

(c) The thresholded scope ties the simple rule: DTH1/INF-r is 0.983 [0.954, 1.012], 0.982 [0.962, 1.005] and 1.044 [1.017, 1.072].

(d) A relay or data-mule mechanism is not the lever. An oracle release broadcast removes about 0 of the REP+→FULL gap (share removed −0.61 to +0.46 across cells). The partition loss is coordination, not news latency.

(e) The planner does not collapse: RH-ALNS vs RH-constructor 0.906 and 0.904, CIs below 1.
- But rolling ALNS under noise alone is no better than open-loop ALNS (1.016, 1.003).
- A cold-restart ALNS churns routes (905 vs 25 versions) and loses to the dispatcher (75.3 vs 49.6 static). Warm start plus coalition commitment are therefore essential parts of the method, not optional.

Prespecified collapse tests (dev → test)
- Planner: SCOPE-RALNS vs the same scope with RH-constructor, with the earliest-start dispatcher, and with the paper greedy. Required: ≤ 0.97, CI < 1, on ≥ 3/4 settings.
- Communication: DTHθ vs INF-r, and vs REP+, CSRc, FRZk, LOC-F. A mechanism is claimed only if it wins by ≥ 2% with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05. The expected outcome is no mechanism claim.
- Decision-divergence log: the share of re-plans where SCOPE's authored versions differ from REP+'s and INF-r's on the same belief, and the share of out-of-reach robots with τ_i − now > 1.
propose-2.pilot_plan:
Day 0 is done. It produced the pilots above: about 6,700 surrogate-world runs plus 800 rolling-horizon runs, each wave taking 1–8 minutes on 16–28 processes.

Week plan (CPU only; ≤ 24 processes; timings on pinned, quiet cores)

- Days 1–2: CommLayer inside DynTaskEnv.
  - Arrival-order coalitions, CRDT beliefs, CRN channel (Bernoulli, GE, Rayleigh), heartbeats.
  - Tests: ideal comm reproduces the static env bit-for-bit for plan replay and RL rollouts; arrival order equals decision order; CRN identical across methods.
- Days 2–3: rolling ALNS inside the comm world.
  - Warm start, within-component commitment, residual heads, ETA leases.
  - Unit check: with ideal comm, static and noise-free, it must be within 1% of the open-loop ALNS plan (today's cold version is 52% worse, which is the bug being fixed).
- Days 3–4: baselines and the RL-dec belief wrapper.
  - CEN-F, REP+, INF-r / DTHθ, RL-dec (obs_from_belief), RH-constructor, dispatcher, CBTA+PR reimplementation.
  - Sanity check CBTA against its paper's qualitative claim (it beats CBGA on average start time).
- Days 5–6: dev campaign.
  - 4 settings × 20 instances × 3 seeds × R/r_c {∞, 1.5, 1.0, 0.75, 0.6} × {RN12, RN3} × about 10 arms, and GE at 1.0 r_c.
- Day 7: analysis against the kill criteria. The prereg (docs/trackD-spec.md) is then frozen and committed by the user.

Kill criteria (dev split)
- K1 (planner): SCOPE-RALNS vs RH-constructor with the same scope at P must be ≤ 0.97 with CI < 1 on ≥ 3/4 settings. Otherwise the dynamic claim collapses to a simple planner: stop Track D as an algorithm and keep only a descriptive robustness appendix.
- K2 (headroom vs central): SCOPE vs CEN-F pooled at P must be ≤ 0.95 with CI < 1. Otherwise central re-solve suffices and C3 is reported as parity.
- K3 (replicated): if REP+ beats SCOPE with CI < 1 at P, switch the default to θ = ∞. This is not a kill, but the method is then literally the replicated solver.
- K4 (mechanism): if the best DTHθ does not beat INF-r by ≥ 2% with p < 0.05, there is no communication-mechanism claim. This is expected.
- K5 (RL strawman): if RL-dec fails more than 20% of runs or degrades more than 50%, also report RL at its best communication arrangement.
- K6 (ranking shift): if the rolling-ALNS ranking of REP+ vs INF-r differs from today's dispatcher-based ranking, re-run the collapse arms before freezing.
propose-2.prereg_endpoints:
Scope and statistics
- Test split: 50 instances per setting × 3 CRN seeds; 4 primary settings; condition P (RN12, R = 1.0 r_c, Bernoulli 0.25).
- Per pair: r = makespan(SCOPE) / makespan(competitor) at the same per-event budget (300 iterations, 1 core); failure counts as 200.
- Report the geometric-mean ratio, paired bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 0) and win counts.

Endpoints
- E1 (C3 superiority): one-sided paired t on mean log r < 0 against CEN-F-RALNS, RL-dec, CBTA-PR-dec and RH-constructor. Holm over 4 settings × 4 competitors, α = 0.05.
- E2 (C3 vs replicated): TOST against REP+ (same ALNS) with margin ±3% (log 1.03), per setting, Holm-adjusted. One-sided superiority is reported but not required.
- E3 (degradation): D = makespan(m, P) / makespan(m, ideal comm), paired. Test D(SCOPE) < D(CEN-F) and D(SCOPE) < D(RL-dec), one-sided, Holm.
- E4 (success): non-inferiority, success(SCOPE) ≥ success(competitor) − 2 pp (one-sided exact paired test).
- E5 (C2 dynamic):
  - Per-event CPU on 1 pinned core: p95 ≤ 0.1 s at 300 iterations; median reported.
  - Anytime curve over {30, 100, 300, 1000} iterations.
  - SCOPE on 1 core vs CEN-F with CP-SAT-LNS on 8 cores at 1 s per event: TOST ±3% or superiority.
- E6 (messages): route-version messages and bytes per robot per time unit vs REP+ and CEN-F (ratio with CI). The pilot suggests INF-r authors about 50% of REP+'s versions under partitions (12.4k vs 24.4k per episode, MA-AT-25, R = 0.1).

Secondary and ablation families
- Secondary (descriptive, Holm within family): R/r_c ∈ {2.0, 1.25, 0.75, 0.6}; GE and Rayleigh channels; RN3 and R1 releases; 10% failures; MA-AT-50-5-200.
- Ablations (mechanism claims only if they survive Holm within the family): DTHθ vs INF-r; ALNS vs constructor in the loop; coalition commitment on vs off; ETA lease vs fixed lease; LWW vs most-informed merge rule.

Decision rule
- Track D supports C3 if E1 holds for CEN-F and RL-dec on ≥ 3/4 settings, E2 or superiority holds for REP+, and E4 holds.
- Otherwise the results are reported descriptively. No Track D algorithm claim is made on 20-task settings.
propose-2.risks:
1. Novelty. By evidence, the communication layer is a simple rule: plan only for robots you can reach, keep only physical commitments, tolerate redundancy. Reviewers will read Track D as an evaluation, not a method.
   - Prior art per axis: CC-OPI (versioned grow-only set, locks), CBTA and CBBA-PR, ADG (key-order deadlock freedom), D-ITAGS (repair), epistemic replanning (Bramblett & Bezzo 2023–24, reasoning about disconnected teammates), and Lott & Honary 2026 (short bundles win under loss).
   - The defensible novelty is empirical: SOTA coalition planning that stays SOTA online over partitioned networks, on an externally anchored benchmark.
2. All communication rankings come from a surrogate world whose planner is roughly RL-level (FULL makespan on MA-AT-25 RN12 is 52–57, versus about 40 for open-loop ALNS under noise). With rolling ALNS, plans are more tightly coupled, and the ranking of REP+ vs INF-r may shift (K6).
3. The rolling-ALNS benefit (about 9.5% over the cold constructor) was measured with global information and noise only. It is unmeasured with releases and partitions. Also, rolling ALNS did not beat open-loop ALNS under noise alone, so re-planning value comes only from releases and communication events.
4. Surrogate artifacts: a fixed lease cap caused cascading abandons; tail failures (the 200 cap) dominate some means. Mitigations: ETA leases, log-ratio statistics with success rate reported separately, and 150 pairs per setting. Pilot CIs were about ±4% at 160 pairs per range.
5. Fidelity of the CBTA reimplementation (no code exists); CV_MRTA channel code has no license (the protocol is reimplemented).
6. The RL-dec strawman risk. RL sees zero-row patterns it never saw in training; RL at its best communication arrangement is also reported.
7. The time-unit mapping (100 s per unit, 1 km square) is a declared convention. The Gilbert-Elliott parameters become nearly i.i.d. per 10 s tick.
8. The station is assumed range-limited. A long-range downlink (oracle release) did not change conclusions in the pilot, which reduces but does not remove this risk.
9. Concurrent edits to cbba_sota by other agents. Pilots import the frozen pilots/trackD/_snap; any production port must pin a commit.
10. Timing noise on a shared host (load 85–110 during the pilots). E5 must run on quiet, pinned cores.
propose-2.guarantees:
Claimed, with modest scope:
- Strong eventual consistency of the replicated state inside any connected component. The CRDT merge is commutative, associative and idempotent; route versions use last-writer-wins on (Lamport epoch, id). Replicas that have received the same event set hold identical state after one flooding round.
- Deadlock-freedom inside a consistent component. Key-ordered minimal-cover plans give an acyclic wait-for graph (the ADG / serial schedule-generation argument). Delays shift times but not precedence.
- Bounded waiting per visit. The ETA lease abandons after the believed latest partner ETA plus margin m. Failed or unreachable partners therefore never block a robot forever.
- Liveness, under an eventual-contact assumption (the rally rule brings every idle, disconnected robot into the station's component): every released task is eventually started, and the episode terminates with probability 1.

Not claimed:
- No safety against duplicate service (redundancy is deliberate).
- No optimality bound.
- No guarantee of improvement over REP+ or INF-r.
- No guarantee of coalition atomicity under loss (Two Generals).

propose-3.name: HALO: a regime-gated replicated coalition ALNS for HeteroMRTA-DX. The station plans only the robots it reaches; other groups plan optimistically; with patient partner leases. (Track D integrated design)
propose-3.benchmark_spec:
HeteroMRTA-DX: HeteroMRTA extended with online task release, execution noise and range-limited lossy links, every stressor tied to an external source.

WHAT STAYS IDENTICAL TO HeteroMRTA (marmotlab @ db51e29, Apache-2.0)
- Instance generator.
- Primary settings: MA-AT-25-5-50, MA-AT-50-5-50, SA-AT-50-5-50, SA-BT-50-5-50. Secondary: MA-AT-50-5-200. RALTestSet is descriptive only.
- Binary traits, additive requirements, minimal covers.
- Speed 0.2 in the unit square; depots.
- Makespan = all tasks finished and every robot back at its depot. MAX_TIME 200 = failure, scored as 200 in every ratio.
- The released RL checkpoint, unmodified. An all-zero row means an unknown task or robot (verified max |dp| 7.8e-7).
- Regression requirement: with all tasks at t=0, no noise and ideal links, the world must reproduce the static env bit for bit. This is already shown for DynTaskEnv; it becomes a test for the new world.
- Splits:
  - test = prereg seeds 100000+1000*idx+i, i<50;
  - dev (500000+...) for all tuning;
  - validation (900000+...) for untuned dry runs.
- 3 CRN seeds per instance, with separate keys for release, noise and channel. Inference uses instance means.

STRESSORS (source in brackets)
(1) Online release. Tasks appear at a dispatch station at (0.5,0.5); robots learn of them only through the station and gossip.
- R-P: degree of dynamism 0.5; arrival times are order statistics on [0,H] with H = 0.5 x the paper's RL(g.) makespan [dynamic VRP convention].
- R-B: task ids <= 20 visible at t=0, then +20 every 10 time units [the authors' reactive-planning demo in the released code].
(2) Execution noise.
- Travel delays: LoRR 2026 Start-Kit DelayGenerator. Each tick, each moving robot starts a delay with probability p, lasting Uniform{min..max} ticks; tick = env dt 0.1 [MIT, checked in the source]. N1 = Start-Kit example (p 0.01, 1-4 ticks); N3 = (0.05, 1-10).
- Durations: mean-preserving lognormal, sigma 0.3. CS-HSSRG-style additive delays (Messing et al., RSS 2023) as a robustness cell.
- Combinations: RN12 = R-P + N1 + sigma; RN3 = R-P + N3 + sigma.
(3) Links among robots and the station.
- Range R is a multiple of the random-geometric-graph connectivity radius r_c(n) = sqrt(ln n/(pi n)), n = robots+1 [Penrose 2003; Gupta-Kumar 1998]. Sweep R/r_c in {inf, 2, 1.5, 1, 0.75, 0.5}.
- Declared physical reading: unit square = 1 km, so r_c = 160-200 m, which matches a 2.4 GHz ground-robot mesh.
- Per-message loss uses the CV_MRTA models (arXiv 2609.13711):
  - Bernoulli p in {0, 0.2, 0.5};
  - Gilbert-Elliott with rho 0.8, pGG = 1-(1-rho)p, pBB = rho+(1-rho)p;
  - Rayleigh with L0 40 dB, eta 3, Ptx 30 dBm, h ~ Exp(1) and CV_MRTA's sensitivity ladder, using the declared metres per unit.
- Two fidelity tiers:
  - T1 (sweeps; what all pilots used): disk graph, per-tick link loss, instant flooding inside a connected component, store-carry-forward.
  - T2 (confirmatory cells): 1 tick per hop, per-message loss, a per-node byte budget, delta gossip. Cross-checked against cbja/network.py on small cases.
(4) Infrastructure factor, applied identically to every method: none (primary) vs a LoRa-class low-rate global state beacon (period P in {1,5}, loss 0.2).
(5) Robot failures (secondary): 2 crash-stop robots at uniform random times, detected only by heartbeat silence.

PRIMARY DEGRADED CONDITIONS (prespecified). The pilots show the ranking of methods flips around the connectivity threshold, so there are two primary cells:
- RN12, T2, GE p=0.2, no beacon, no failures, at R = 1.0 r_c ("threshold");
- the same at R = 0.5 r_c ("fragmented").
The full R sweep is reported as curves.

INFORMATION MODEL
- Ground truth is kept separate from each node's copy of the shared state (its replica). Physics runs in continuous time.
- A task starts when the robots present cover its requirement (arrival order). Late or redundant arrivals skip it and count as wasted trips.
- RL and greedy act on their own belief through obs_from_belief, with the checkpoint unchanged.

METRICS
- Makespan (failure = 200) and success.
- Ratio to FULL (the same method with ideal links) and to a clairvoyant ALNS that knows realized durations and release times (reference only).
- Wasted trips, abandons, idle time.
- Route versions, messages and bytes per robot per time unit.
- Per-robot CPU per re-plan (p50/p95) and per time unit.

CODE BASIS
- World: pilots/trackD/integ_headroom.py, subclassed in pilots/trackD_integ/{cas_pilot,decomp_pilot,pb_pilot}.py.
- DynTaskEnv: pilots/trackD/dyn_env.py.
- State-start ALNS kernel: pilots/trackD/rh_kernels.py.
propose-3.algorithm_spec:
HALO (Hub-Anchored, Locally Optimistic). Every node, robot or station, runs the same code; the station has more cores.

1 SHARED STATE (a merge-by-maximum replica, i.e. CBBA-style max-consensus on time-stamped records)
- Tasks:
  - released: grow-only set with the task data;
  - started: earliest (time, coalition) wins;
  - finished: earliest time wins;
  - abandons: grow-only set of (robot, task, epoch).
- Robots: one state record per robot, newest by the robot's own counter wins: mode, target, ETA or predicted finish, position, route hash, adopted plan version. Heartbeat every 1.0 time unit.
- Plans: latest route per robot; newest by (Lamport clock, author) wins.
- Every robot stores and forwards everything (store-carry-forward).
- T2 gossip: on link-up, exchange per-class version digests, then send missing deltas in priority order: robot records, then starts/finishes, then releases, then plan versions.

2 TEAMMATE MODEL
- Robots in the planner's connected component use their fresh records.
- A robot b outside it is assumed to be still doing what its freshest record says, and not free before now: free_b = max(recorded ETA or finish, now), located at its recorded target.
- No roll-forward along b's route. In pilot P4, optimistic dead reckoning predicted b's current task correctly 28% of the time versus 52% for the plain snapshot, and cost 20-28% makespan.
- Travel times are scaled by kappa = 1/(1 - expected stall fraction) of the declared delay model.

3 WHO PLANS
Each component elects a leader from heartbeats: the station if it is in the component, else the lowest robot id.
- Station ("hub") component: plans only the robots in the component. Robots outside keep their believed routes (frozen), and their traits still count toward the coalitions they are believed to be in. This is exactly central re-solve with frozen fallback.
- Any other component:
  - plans ALL robots on its replica using the teammate model;
  - writes route versions for all of them. Versions for absent robots travel by store-carry-forward and are adopted on contact. In pilot P8, writing only the component's own routes was worse in every cell.
  - Regime gate: it re-plans only if the hub-component fraction its members last observed while inside it is below theta, or a member is idle with an empty route. Otherwise it keeps the station's plan. theta is tuned on dev (0.7 in the pilot).
- Trigger: any change in knowledge, else every 1.0 time unit.
- Hysteresis: a new plan is adopted only if nominal makespan improves by >= 0.5%, or it repairs an invalid or unassigned task.

4 PLANNER
- The Phase-1 anytime coalition ALNS with the state-start kernel (rh_kernels.py): per-robot ready times, first leg from the current position, release times honoured.
- Tasks a robot has departed to, is waiting at or is working on are fixed anchors with fixed members.
- Warm start = the current plan restricted to open tasks.
- Iteration budget sized for p95 <= 0.2 s on 1 core at 50 tasks (<= 1 s at 200 tasks).
- Deterministic seed = hash of the replica digest, so identical replicas compute identical plans.
- Minimal covers plus a global key order give exact env semantics, and a consistent plan executes without deadlock.

5 EXECUTION
- Follow the adopted route in key order; coalitions start in arrival order.
- Patient causal lease: a waiting robot abandons only if (it has waited >= g and knows of no partner still coming) or it has waited >= L. Pilot values g=3, L=30; in the full study they are tuned per method on dev from one shared grid. An abandoning robot publishes an abandon event and moves on.
- Rally: an idle robot outside the hub component moves toward the station.
- A robot that knows every task is finished goes home.

6 OPTIONAL: if a long-range channel exists, robot records also ride on it (same merge rule).

LINEAGE, STATED PLAINLY
- CBBA's two phases map loosely onto this design: bundle building becomes replicated ALNS over the whole team, and consensus becomes max-merge on time-stamped records, with plan last-writer-wins playing the role of the timestamped winner table.
- Multi-robot task slots (CBGA/CBTA) become minimal covers.
- There are no iterative auction rounds. Every consistency step tried in the pilots (coalition locks, component-local repair, staleness gates) cost makespan.
propose-3.baselines:
All baselines run in the same DX world with the same channel, the same replica, gossip and store-carry-forward, and the same rally rule. Each method's lease is tuned on dev from one shared grid {g in 0.3,1,3} x {L in 10,30,60}; the pilot showed lease patience alone can flip the sign of REP vs central. Every planner-based method uses the same ALNS kernel and per-event budget unless the budget is the variable being tested.

(B1) CEN-RH: central rolling-horizon ALNS at the station (8 cores, 2 s per event), plans delivered over the mesh. Robots out of reach follow their last route, then a local fallback chosen on dev per setting from {idle, fixed paper greedy, rally}. Pilot proxy: CEN-F. Variant CEN-R: the station re-plans everyone and routes travel by store-carry-forward.

(B2) REP-v: DGA-style replicated solver. Every component leader re-plans all robots; versions are flooded, newest wins; teammates modelled by stale snapshots. Pilot: REP.

(B3) REP-v+clamp: B2 with HALO's teammate model. This is the strongest replicated solver and the equivalence target. Pilot: CLAMP.

(B4) REP-e: DMCHBA-style knowledge flooding; each robot solves the problem and follows only its own part, with no plan messages. Pilot proxy HYB2 was worse than HYB in every cell.

(B5) Coalition auctions with the same gossip, both declared reimplementations (no official code exists):
- CBTA-style timetable consensus (RA-L 2022), makespan objective, re-auction on events;
- CBGA-style grouping auction.

(B6) Published RL(g.) online on beliefs: checkpoint unchanged, zero rows for unknown tasks and robots, observations built from the clamped belief. Also RL(g.) with oracle global state as a reference. RL(s.N) is not a legal online policy under noise and is not used.

(B7) Fixed paper greedy, online on beliefs (the repo greedy has the dist bug).

(B8) OPEN: the t=0 ALNS plan executed open loop with leases; the station inserts released tasks.

References, not competitors:
- FULL: HALO with ideal links.
- Knowledge oracles REP-AO and REP-KO.
- Clairvoyant ALNS.
- Oracle regime switch: per condition, the better of B1 and B3. HALO's gate tries to match it without knowing R.
propose-3.why_it_should_win:
Honest answer: HALO will not beat the strongest baseline by a clear margin everywhere. It is built to tie central re-solve + fallback at or above the connectivity threshold and to beat it clearly below it.

PILOT EVIDENCE
Source: /home/jovyan/dev/cbba-sota/pilots/trackD_integ/out/summary.txt, blocks P2-P8. Setup: list-scheduling planner, 4 dev settings x 10 instances x 2 CRN seeds, 20% per-link loss, every method on the same patient lease. Numbers are makespan HALO/competitor, first RN12 then RN3.

(a) vs central + frozen fallback. HALO in the pilot = HYB3 with theta 0.7.

| Range | RN12 | RN3 |
|---|---|---|
| R=0.3 (1.5-1.9 r_c) | 1.019 [0.998, 1.048] | 0.986 [0.966, 1.003] |
| R=0.2 (~r_c) | 1.017 [0.970, 1.064] | 1.034 [0.991, 1.084] |
| R=0.15 | 0.949 [0.894, 1.005] | 0.959 [0.918, 0.999] |
| R=0.1 (0.5-0.64 r_c) | 0.865 [0.809, 0.923] | 0.813 [0.755, 0.873] |

Why: when the station reaches only 5-35% of robots, stranded groups keep working with the best local knowledge, and their plans reach other robots by store-carry-forward. The anchored station never overrides robots it cannot reach, and the gate stops small stragglers from re-planning when the network is mostly connected. Ungated optimistic replication (CLAMP) is 3-7% worse than central at R >= r_c.

(b) vs the best replicated solver with the same teammate model and lease (REP-v+clamp):
- No advantage at severe fragmentation: against central at R=0.1, HALO-like HYB is 0.838 and CLAMP is 0.839.
- Better near the threshold (R=0.2: 1.017 vs 1.065) because the station is anchored.
- Expected result: equivalence (TOST) at 0.5 r_c and a small edge at r_c.

(c) vs the published RL online: the static gap persists under noise (open-loop ALNS/RL 1.18-1.42 in the earlier trackD pilot), so the expected advantage is 20-30%, mostly solver quality. Not yet run in the comm world.

(d) vs CBTA/CBGA-style auctions: probably >= 10% (myopic bundles plus consensus latency). Unverified, and these are reimplementations.

(e) vs OPEN (no re-planning): 26-51% better.

WHERE THE GAINS COME FROM (also a paper result)
- Stale knowledge of teammates' current state is the bottleneck:
  - a teammate-state oracle takes REP from 1.101 to 0.996 of FULL at R=0.2 and from 1.505 to 1.083 at R=0.1;
  - a release oracle closes about 0% of the gap;
  - a task-status-only oracle makes things worse (1.29-2.03).
- A cheap global state beacon (period 1, 20% loss) improves REP by 8%, 13-15% and 23-27% at R = 0.2 / 0.15 / 0.1.
- Lease patience (max wait 10 -> 30) improves REP by 5-17% and cuts abandons about 10x.
- Consistency mechanisms (coalition locks CAS, component-local repair LOC-F, staleness gate SG) and schedule slack (q80/SAA lever 1.000-1.02) do not help.

BOTTOM LINE
The defensible C3 claim is: non-inferior to central at r_c (5% margin), about 10-15% better at 0.5 r_c, equivalent to the best replicated solver, and far better than the published RL.

HALO costs more messages, not fewer: it writes about 2x the route versions of central at R=0.3 and up to about 170x at R=0.1. The draft C3 clause "uses fewer messages" must be dropped.
propose-3.collapse_check:
HALO is mostly a composition of simple rules, and the proposal says so up front. The pilots found five levers, each nearly a one-liner:
1. patient partner leases;
2. clamped teammate snapshot;
3. asymmetric scope: station conservative, stranded groups optimistic;
4. regime gate on the observed station-component fraction;
5. rally to the station when idle and disconnected.
What is interesting is why these are the levers: staleness of teammate state dominates, redundant coverage is cheap when coalitions form in arrival order, and consistency is expensive. The CBBA-lineage consistency machinery was null or harmful in every pilot (CAS locks, LOC-F, SG gates), so it is kept only as ablations.

ANALYTIC LIMITS (each prespecified as a TOST check)
- R -> inf: the station component contains everyone, so HALO equals CEN-RH exactly (TOST +-1% at R = 2 r_c).
- theta -> 0: HALO equals central + frozen fallback.
- theta -> 1 with station anchoring off: HALO equals REP-v+clamp.
- So the gate interpolates between two baselines. The real question is whether it matches the per-condition oracle switch without knowing R.

PRESPECIFIED COLLAPSE TESTS (dev first, then test)
(1) Oracle-switch test: HALO vs the per-condition better of {CEN-RH, REP-v+clamp}.
- Within 2% everywhere: the contribution is "an online regime detector plus the diagnosis".
- More than 3% below the better one in any primary cell: HALO is a compromise, and the paper says so.
(2) 2^4 factorial at both primary ranges on {patient lease, clamp, station anchoring, gate}, plus a gossip knockout (no relay or store-carry-forward) and a rally knockout. Report main effects and interactions. If one factor explains >= 80% of the HALO-vs-central effect, the paper states "HALO collapses to rule X".
(3) Decision-diff log: the share of dispatch decisions where HALO differs from CEN-RH and from REP-v+clamp, per range.
(4) Planner swap: ALNS vs list scheduling inside both HALO and CEN-RH, to separate architecture from solver quality.
(5) Falsification: if any consistency mechanism improves HALO by more than 2% on dev, the "redundancy beats consistency" claim is dropped.
(6) Slack: q80 durations or SAA inside HALO, TOST +-1%; expected null (lever 1.000-1.02).
propose-3.prereg_endpoints:
CONFIRMATORY SETUP (test split)
- 4 primary settings x 50 instances x 3 CRN seeds; T2 world, RN12, GE 0.2, no beacon.
- theta, leases, fallbacks and ALNS budget frozen from dev; commit hashes recorded.
- Unit = instance mean over seeds. Statistic = paired log-ratio of makespans (failure = 200).
- Report the mean ratio with bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 0) and win counts.
- Holm correction across the 4 settings within each hypothesis; pooled estimates are the headlines.

C3 (NETWORK ROBUSTNESS)
- H3a fragmented (R = 0.5 r_c): HALO < CEN-RH with its best fallback. One-sided paired t, alpha 0.05. Expected about 0.85.
- H3b threshold (R = 1.0 r_c): HALO non-inferior to CEN-RH with a 5% margin (ratio < 1.05, one-sided). Expected 0.98-1.03. A 3% margin is secondary and expected to fail at per-setting power.
- H3c degradation: the paired area under log(makespan / own FULL) over R/r_c in {2, 1.5, 1, 0.75, 0.5} is smaller for HALO than for CEN-RH.
- H3d vs the strongest replicated solver (REP-v+clamp): TOST +-3% pooled at each primary range. Superiority is claimed only if the one-sided test is significant.
- H3e success rate: non-inferior to every baseline, 2 percentage-point margin.
- Messages and bytes are reported as costs. There is no claim of fewer messages than central.

C2 (LOW COMPUTE / ANYTIME)
- H2a: per-event re-plan CPU p95 <= 0.2 s on 1 core at 50 tasks and <= 1.0 s at 200 tasks (threshold, full distribution reported).
- H2b anytime saturation: HALO at 0.2 s vs 2 s per event, TOST +-2% at both primary ranges.
- H2c light vs heavy: HALO (1 core per robot, 0.2 s) non-inferior within 2% to CEN-RH (8 cores, 2 s) at ideal links. Declared mapping 1 time unit = 100 s, so solver latency is charged but negligible.
- H2d: HALO with ALNS beats HALO with list scheduling at both ranges.

SECONDARY (Holm within family)
- HALO vs RL(g.) online on beliefs, CBTA-style, CBGA-style, fixed greedy and OPEN (superiority).
- RN3, R-B release, Bernoulli 0.5, Rayleigh.
- 2 crash failures.
- Beacon factor, applied to all methods.
- Wasted trips and abandons; the factorial ablation.

The shipped RALTestSet and the dev and validation splits are descriptive only.
propose-3.risks:
1. Regime dependence (main risk). The decentralized advantage exists only below the connectivity threshold; at R >= r_c, central + fallback with patient leases ties or wins by 2-7% unless the gate works. Reviewers may call 0.5 r_c contrived. Mitigations: the physical mapping (1 km site, 2.4 GHz ground mesh at 100-300 m), the full R curve, and the 1 km figures stated openly.

2. Collapse to simple rules. Every lever that helped is nearly a one-liner, and the CBBA-lineage consistency components were null or harmful. The method novelty is thin; the paper leans on the benchmark, the Phase-1 ALNS, the diagnostic decomposition, and an honest factorial.

3. Tuning sensitivity. Lease patience flipped the sign of REP vs central (short lease: REP 5% better; patient lease: central 3-4% better at r_c). Per-method dev tuning on one shared grid and sensitivity curves are mandatory. theta was picked post hoc from 2 values on dev, so it must be frozen on dev and confirmed on test.

4. Pilot fidelity.
- A list-scheduling planner stood in for ALNS; with ALNS the gaps may shrink or grow.
- T1 floods instantly inside a component, which overstates gossip; T2 may shrink the replicated advantage.
- Per-cell CIs were +-4-6% at 40 instances.

5. Baseline fairness.
- RL on stale beliefs is outside its training distribution and may collapse, which reads as a strawman; the oracle-state RL is reported alongside.
- CBTA and CBGA have no code; reimplementation fidelity may be disputed.

6. Infrastructure caveat. A LoRa-class state beacon recovers 8-27% for any replicated method. Where such a channel exists, the degraded-network problem largely disappears, so the C3 story applies to short-range-only deployments and must say so.

7. Messages. HALO sends about 2-170x more route versions than central. C3's "fewer messages" wording has to go.

8. C2 motivation is weak online. At plausible physical scales 1 time unit is about 100 s, so solver latency never limits makespan; C2 becomes an argument about per-robot CPU and energy, not reaction time.

9. Design choices not taken from HeteroMRTA: station at the centre, release at the station, rally rule, arrival-order coalitions. Add a sensitivity run with a corner station.

10. Prior art. Epistemic teammate prediction (Bramblett & Bezzo, arXiv 2302.10393 and 2308.00579), CC-OPI (2609.19208), CV_MRTA (2609.13711), bundle length under loss (2609.06273), D-ITAGS repair, ADG ordering. Novelty is only in the combination and the evidence.

11. Engineering. Other agents edit cbba_sota concurrently (pilots import a frozen _snap copy), and the shared host ran at load above its 96-CPU quota, so wall-clock numbers from these pilots are not valid timing measurements.
propose-3.guarantees:
- Knowledge convergence. Each node's replica merges by taking maxima or unions (grow-only sets, earliest-time registers, newest-wins registers with a total tie-break), so it is strongly eventually consistent: two nodes that received the same updates hold identical state, and with the deterministic seed they compute identical plans. If every pair of nodes is linked infinitely often through time-respecting relay paths, every event reaches every node in finite time. The rally rule makes idle disconnected robots approach the station; it supports this condition but does not prove it.

- Safe execution. A consistent key-ordered minimal-cover plan executes without deadlock under any finite delays: the precedence graph follows the global key order, as in the RCPSP serial schedule-generation scheme and ADG. Under inconsistent plans (partitions), every wait is bounded by L, so no robot waits forever. An abandon can only raise a task's remaining requirement, and any node that learns of it re-plans the task.

- Completion (a proposition still to be proven). If the surviving robots can cover every requirement and contacts recur, every released task finishes in finite time.

- No optimality or approximation guarantee. ALNS is a heuristic; FULL and the clairvoyant ALNS are empirical references only.

- Cost.
  - Per re-plan: O(iterations x tasks x robots) numba work, capped by the iteration budget.
  - Per-robot replica: O(tasks + robots) records.
  - Messages: O(events + robots x heartbeat rate), plus plan versions, which were measured at about 2-170x central for R <= 1.9 r_c.
